assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural empirical models of demand and competition have transformed industrial-organization analysis and policy-relevant measurement.
assessment.attribution: Pakes, Berry and Bresnahan are central architects of the linked empirical framework, though the candidate framing encompasses a wider group.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been extensively adopted across industries and have a long record of substantive applications.
uncertainties: The broad contribution and seven-person credit list make a three-person attribution necessarily incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The formal analysis of trade policy and political incentives supplied a durable framework for understanding protection.
assessment.attribution: Helpman and Grossman are the clearly delimited credited pair for this theoretical contribution.
assessment.maturity: The work is longstanding, foundational and continues to organize research on political economy of trade.
uncertainties: Its empirical reach is less direct than that of some applied candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection fundamentally changed modern trade theory and measurement of trade gains.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is indispensable to the core framework; Helpman and Redding made major complementary contributions to its development and application.
assessment.maturity: The framework is deeply integrated into theoretical and empirical international-trade work.
uncertainties: The precise division between the core innovation and subsequent extensions remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Economic analysis of network effects, digital markets and information goods has had exceptional and lasting practical importance.
assessment.attribution: Shapiro, Varian and Katz are major foundational contributors, although Farrell and Athey also represent important elements of the broad listed field.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been tested through decades of research and are central to modern competition analysis.
uncertainties: The candidate description aggregates several related contributions and makes exclusive attribution difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods made credible empirical analysis feasible in a vast range of economic applications.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond provided the defining estimator, with Blundell a central contributor to its major extension.
assessment.maturity: The methods are longstanding, highly influential and subject to extensive methodological scrutiny and refinement.
uncertainties: Widespread misuse in applications complicates assessment of the contribution's practical record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The study of risk sharing and informal insurance established a powerful account of household behavior and institutions in poor rural economies.
assessment.attribution: Townsend supplied foundational theory and evidence, while Udry and Rosenzweig made central empirical and institutional contributions.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has produced a long-lived body of evidence and influenced development economics broadly.
uncertainties: The external validity of village-based evidence and the boundaries of shared credit merit continued care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evolutionary accounts of routines and firm capabilities offer a distinctive, influential explanation of organizational change and economic dynamism.
assessment.attribution: Winter is the sole credited candidate and a central figure in the stated intellectual program.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has shaped a large interdisciplinary literature over many decades.
uncertainties: The field's diffuse boundaries and reliance on a broader intellectual tradition complicate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework provided a compelling quantitative lens on productivity and cross-country income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Restuccia and Klenow are appropriately identified as principal contributors to the stated agenda.
assessment.maturity: The approach has generated extensive follow-on research and policy-relevant measurement exercises.
uncertainties: Inference about distortions from residual dispersion is model-dependent, and causal interpretation remains debated.
